$comment: Every number the character is built from lives here so the review loop can tune it.
Units are metres. Frame: Y up, origin on the floor midway between the feet, the
character facing +Z. +X is her LEFT, which is screen-right in the front view --
her tattooed arm and the pouch are on +X.
Heights are absolute above the floor and were read off ref/views/clay_2.png and
clay_0.png with tools/grid.py; see docs/MEASUREMENTS.md.

meta.name: Jinx
meta.source: Thibaut Granet - ARCANE - Jinx - Modeling & Texturing

widths.$comment: Half-widths (x) and half-depths (z) at the named height.

pose.$comment: Measured off clay_2: her LEFT foot's lowest pixel sits 0.047 m above her RIGHT foot's, so she stands with the weight on her right leg and the left one raised and a little forward. stanceHalfW 0.052 was chosen by A/B on the composite score (41.6 against 40.9 at 0.058), NOT by the earlier claim that the reference's legs touch down to y = 0.22 -- that claim was wrong. The front silhouette reads as one run there because a BRAID bridges the gap, not because the calves meet; zoom clay_2 between y 0.62 and 0.22 and the backdrop is visible between them.

$comment: Head measured off ref/views/head_1.png (front) and head_2.png (profile).
head_1 scales at 2646 px/m from landmarks eye=1.584 and chin=1.505, with
the midline at column 425 and the eye line at row 338.
Read from it: pupil separation 0.0605, eye aperture 0.0299 x 0.0121 with
the outer canthus 0.0076 above the inner, iris 0.0140 across, nose wing
width 0.0227, mouth 0.0356 across, lips 1.518..1.531 with the lip line at
face half-width 0.0593 at eye level, 0.0574 at 1.561, 0.0522 at 1.542,
From head_2 the nose tip is 12.6 mm forward of the chin front and the lips
sit 6.5 mm behind the tip, 6 mm ahead of the chin.
sections[] is the skull loft and frontLoft[] the shallower stack that
flattens the plane of the face; both are [y, halfX, zFront, zBack, ry]
ellipsoid slices. An ellipse alone puts the surface 5 mm behind where the
eyeball has to sit, which is what makes eyes read as stuck on -- hence the
second stack. Both are kept MONOTONIC in zFront and their ry at least
twice the slice spacing: a slice thinner than that scallops, and the
scallop lands on the forehead as corduroy. The brow overhang and the eye
socket are therefore cut with orbit[] rather than lofted.
ROUND 3. Every band on this face is 3-11 mm wide and materials are picked
per VERTEX, so a band narrower than a voxel comes out as a row of blocks.
Two answers, both applied here:
(a) the eyeballs left the head shell and became their own, at
eyeVoxelScale 0.16 -- 1.7 mm at the low LOD, so a 14 mm iris is 8
samples across instead of 3, and the lash line can be PAINTED on the
globe (lashT/lashSkew) instead of floating as a slab;
(b) every remaining band was given real relief, so the boundary has a
crease for the vertices to land on: browRidge is now a proud ridge
(ridgeRInner/ridgeBack, pushed in along `inward` rather than in -z so
it follows the skull), the lips are two separate masses split by a
3 mm groove, and mento[] is the mentolabial crease the profile was
missing.
The aperture is a LENS -- two big circles intersected -- not an ellipsoid,
because an ellipsoid has no corner and the reference's outer canthus is a
sharp flick. apHalfW/apHalfH are the lens half-axes and the circle radius
falls out as (a*a + b*b) / (2b).
A ridge, not a decal. The tube is pushed ridgeBack along the direction
from the curve point toward `inward` -- i.e. roughly along the inward
surface normal of the skull, which -z alone is not once x passes 30 mm.
What shows is a band 2*sqrt(r^2 - ridgeBack^2) wide standing
(r - ridgeBack) proud: 11.0 mm wide and 2.0 mm proud at the inner end,
5.8 mm and 0.6 mm at the tail. That matches the reference band
1.598..1.609 and gives the paint a crease to stop against.
Two masses, not one. The round-2 lips had both tubes at y ~ 1.524, so
there was no upper/lower and the paint was a slab. Upper spans
1.5248..1.5312, lower 1.5167..1.5247, and the seam between them is a
3.2 mm groove -- wide enough to survive the low LOD's voxel, which the
old 2.4 mm one was not.

mento.$comment: Mentolabial crease -- without it the chin has no edge in profile and the whole lower face reads as one lump.

ear.$comment: Round 2's ear was a plate with a bowl bitten out and at the low LOD the bowl read as a hole; round 3's first try added a helix, antihelix and tragus but at 2.4-3.3 mm they were under one voxel and shredded. These are the same features at 3.6-4.2 mm with a 4 mm blend -- coarse enough to survive, which is the only kind of ear detail worth having here.

$comment: Measured off the turnaround; the tables live in src/parts/hair.ts and the
derivation is in its header.  Only tuning scalars are carried here.
The panel x measurements are taken about the MIRROR-FIT body midline, not
the alpha-bbox centre: the braids pull the bbox centre 14.8 mm off the
midline in clay_2 and 14.3 mm the other way in clay_5, and reading widths
off the bbox frame is what made the previous pass symmetric.
braidTurns 16: the lobe pitch on clay_5 is ~0.032 m over a 1.53 m braid,
and a 3-strand plait shows 3 lobes per turn, so 3*turns = 48.
ROUND 2.  braid_area_frac at yaw 90/270 was 0.115 against a reference
0.044/0.034.  Measured run by run at yaw 90, that was NOT thickness: the
braid run was 0.034-0.060 against the reference's 0.034-0.049.  It was
standoff -- the plait hung 7 to 37 mm clear of the back from y 0.3 to 1.5,
so it read as its own thin silhouette run and `debraid` discarded all of
it, while clay_0 is ONE run from y 0.70 to the crown.  The fix is in the
z column of BRAID_ROWS (probed off the assembled body with
out/hair_backz.ts), not in braidR0.
ROUND 3.  crestWideX and crestBlend are gone: the crest is no longer a pair
of squashed cone chains but a loft of ellipses solved from the four widths
the six panels actually measure (CROWN_ROWS in hair.ts).  crownBlend and
massBlend keep the values this fragment already carried -- every round-3
measurement was taken with them -- and the code defaults now agree.
fringeClip is how far the forward fringe may stand outside the solved crown
ellipse; it is what stops five hand-placed locks from being measured as
crown at yaw 315.  furrowR is the radius of the layer grooves cut along the
blade: at 0.0055, sunk to 0.8 of the half thickness, they serrated the top.
Black halter crop top.  Round 2.  Heights and widths re-read off
ref/views/body_2.png with the metre grid keyed to the panel's alpha bbox
(sole = 0, hairTip = 1.715 -> 743.44 px/m) and the body centreline at
x = 195 px.  The centreline is confirmed by the choker, which is symmetric
about it: at y = 1.450 the dark wrap runs -0.048..+0.046 and at y = 1.440
-0.058..+0.062.  (The boots are NOT on that centreline -- their midpoint
sits ~32 mm to her right at 171 px -- so do not derive it from the feet.)
ROUND 1 DEFECTS FIXED HERE
1. The cut edge was a single plane, i.e. a straight oblique chord, and it
was 8..15 mm too wide over the whole ribcage.  Classifying the front
panel into skin / black cloth gives the cloth's outer edge, her right
(the side her arm does not overlap):
and her left, where the arm crowds it: .090 .090 .086 .079 .074 .067
.063 .065 .066.  Read the other way -- the highest cloth in each column
which agrees with the row scan to a pixel.  So the edge is a CURVE: its
slope is ~0 up to y = 1.30 and rises to 0.75 by y = 1.38.  `edge` is
that curve, a monotone-cubic table of half-width against height, and it
replaces armEdgeX/Y/Z/Slope.  The numbers in it are the plane constant,
not the silhouette: the z-tilt (armEdgeDepth) adds up to 38 mm at the
front, so the table is fitted against the baked shell, iterating on the
probe in out/top_probe.ts.
2. The neck strap was a slab of constant half-width 0.060 butted onto the
bib, so the neckline had a right-angle notch at (0.060, 1.375) -- very
visible at yaw 45.  `collar` is now a curve too, and it continues the
bib's silhouette (0.061 at 1.380 -> 0.052 at the top) instead of
stepping off it.  It is also offset by collarX, because the reference's
cloth span at the throat is not centred on the spine: -0.051..+0.062 at
the slab centred on x = 0 and the opening off centre at +0.016, her left
strap came out 5 mm wide -- a spike, not a strap.  Built, the straps are
3. The strap's top was a flat horizontal cut at y = 1.4315 that read as a
ledge.  It is now rounded (collarRound) AND lifted to 1.4365, inside
the choker's lowest wrap (1.4333..1.4437), with the cloth offset thinned
from 9 mm to 5.8 mm between y = 1.400 and y = 1.430 (neckThin*) so the
strap's outer radius there, 0.0430 + 0.0058 = 0.0488, clears under the
wrap's outer radius of 0.0499.  That is what the reference shows: the
straps run under the choker rather than stopping against it.
4. The brass keeper loop on the hem band was never modelled.  It is at
x = -0.048..-0.039, y = 1.231..1.251 on the sheet -- a 9 mm brass bar
wrapping the band, mirroring the steel buckle frame at +0.018..+0.046.
Built 12 mm wide because 9 mm is under one low-LOD voxel.
NECKLINE.  The opening is a rounded V that widens as it climbs, not a
constant-width slot, and it is off centre toward her left:
so neckOpenX 0.016, half-width 0.0125 at the bottom flaring at 0.60 and
clamped at 0.031 (above y = 1.4333 the choker covers everything anyway).
The cloth is one run at y = 1.380 (-0.059..+0.063) and two at 1.390, so
the scoop bottoms out at y = 1.3865.
HEM AND BAND.  The cloth's bottom edge is at y = 1.2246 at the centreline
and 1.2219..1.2259 out to |x| = 0.065, i.e. flat, not the 1.218 round 1
used.  The band's seam is at y = 1.250, so the band is 1.2240..1.2495.
The reference's band edge is at |x| = 0.101, the same as the bib's, so
underBandProud comes down from 8 mm to 3 mm.
LACING.  Re-checked, unchanged.  Brass eyelet centres off the brass mask:
cluster spans x -0.052..+0.049 and y 1.300..1.372.  The built cross spans
laceThick/ringThick are NOT the reference's thicknesses, they are the depth
needed to survive the mesher: at 5 mm the diagonals fall under one low-LOD
voxel and the X bakes as an H.
BACK.  clay_5 / body_5 show a bare upper back, skin from the shoulders down
to the band.  backZ0/backSlope bite that opening out of the bib only; the
collar is exempt, because the halter's strap really does ring the neck --
body_5 has a dark band at the nape at y = 1.44.
PROXY.  The garment hangs on a copy of body.ts's trunk and it has to stay a
copy: in round 1 the copy had drifted -- it still expected body.trap to be
a capsule (x0/y0/z0..) when body.ts had made it an ellipsoid (cx/cy/cz,
rx/ry/rz), so the proxy silently dropped the trapezius altogether -- the
shoulder mass that reaches x = 0.099 at y = 1.420 where the yoke column on
its own is only 0.053, a 46 mm hole in the surface the collar hangs on --
and it
used a hand-written bust and a smootherstep loft where body.ts uses
body.bust and a Fritsch-Carlson one.  Fixed here.  If body.yoke, body.trap,
body.bust or body.blend* move, this moves with them.
BUDGET.  voxelScale was 0.68 in round 1: a 3.1 mm voxel at --lod high and
62.7 k triangles, 12% of the whole character's budget for one garment.
0.80 is 3.6 mm / 44.7 k, and the X lacing still reads at the low LOD's
8.4 mm voxel because paint() carries its colour even where the mesher
rounds the ridge off.
Three leather wraps round the throat with a shallow X crossing the front,
read off ref/views/body_2.png and ref/views/head_1.png.
ROUND 2.  Re-measured on the front panel with the metre grid (743.44 px/m,
centreline 195 px).  The wraps' centres are y = 1.4385, 1.4545 and 1.4685
and each is ~9 mm tall, so the stack runs 1.4335..1.4735 -- 40 mm, not the
45 mm round 1 built.  Its half-width there is 0.047 (the dark run at
y = 1.450 is -0.048..+0.046) against a bare neck of 0.044 just above it, so
the leather is only ~3 mm proud and `thickness` must stay small.
At round 1's voxelScale 0.5 -- a 5.3 mm voxel -- the three wraps and the X
fused into one dark blob: the gaps between wraps are 4..6 mm, i.e. under
one voxel.  0.38 (a 4.0 mm voxel) is what lets the gaps read, and it is the
cheapest place on the character to spend triangles because the choker is
small.  The choker was also invisible in round 1 -- it baked inside a 137 mm
ball body.ts had at the throat -- which body.json's measured `yoke` has
since fixed; it is now the outermost surface at the neck.
neck* mirrors head.json's neck column extended down to y = 1.420, which is
the same column body.json's yoke now carries (r 0.0435 at 1.420 tapering to
0.040 at 1.525).  neckInset sinks every piece 6 mm into it so the shell is
13 mm thick and survives the voxel; only the outer 5-9 mm shows.
The top's neck straps pass UNDER this stack: top.json thins their standoff
to 5.8 mm above y = 1.430 so their outer radius, 0.0488, clears the lowest
wrap's 0.0499.  If `gap` or `thickness` here drop, top.neckThinBy has to
grow to match or the strap's cut end pokes through the leather.
Purple pinstripe capris. Numbers read off ref/views/body_2.png and body_5.png
with the metre grid; see the pants section of the part report.
waistY: top of the waistband, read at 1.086 on the +X hip in body_2.
hemY + hemSideOffset[side] is the LOWEST point of that leg's rag, at the BACK of
the leg; tatterFrontRise then lifts it toward the front by that much again.
flare: [height, metres of cloth standoff from the body's own leg radius].
ROUND 2: the flare over the leg was 15-19 mm, which read as jodhpurs and cost
+22% on the back view's core run and +34/39% on the two side views' leg depth.
body_2's matte keeps the inseam open (clay_2's bridges it), and her right leg --
the wider of the two, and therefore the one the widest-run width term reads --
That difference is a flat +6 mm, so that is what the table now carries below y=0.72;
from 0.78 up the reference's own outline there is the sash low corner, not the
trouser, so the blouse over the seat is left close to where round 1 measured it.
ROUND 3. The round-2 brief read the side views at hip height and concluded the
leg was too SHALLOW. It is the other way round below the knee, and the number it
read was braids. Measured off the CLAY panels with tools/pants_probe.py, which
normalises exactly as compare.py does, and off the pants-only render in world
metres with tools/pants_abs.py:
LEG DEPTH, the single leg run in the two side panels (clay_4 front-most run,
clay_0 leg run; the other run in clay_4 is a braid hanging free behind her,
not a second leg -- clay_0 shows the legs at the same z, so there is no stride):
y      clay_4   clay_0   render
so the trouser is 26-32 mm too deep at the calf and correct at the thigh: the
taper in z was missing entirely. `flareZ` splits the standoff off `flare` and
takes it to 1 mm below the knee, where the body's own shin (squashZ 1.18) is
already deeper than the reference's whole leg run.
LEG SPAN ACROSS, outer edge to outer edge of the pair:
y      clay_2   clay_5   render
and clay_5, whose matte keeps the inseam open, splits it into her right leg
0.106/0.106/0.108 and her left 0.087/0.082/0.091 with a 42-45 mm gap between
them. Our gap is 43 mm, so the gap is right and each leg is ~13 mm short on
its OUTER edge. `legOut` hangs the tube that far outboard of the bone and
widens it by the same, which moves only the outer edge: predicted right leg
0.103, left 0.088, span 0.235 against the reference's 0.106/0.082/0.234.
HEM HEIGHT. The build's own hem convention is
base(theta) = hemY + hemSideOffset[side] + tatterDepth + rise*(0.5+0.5cos)
with the teeth cutting up to tatterDepth off that, so the FRONT of a leg runs
from hemY+offset+rise (deepest tooth) to that plus tatterDepth. At hemY 0.466
that put her right leg's front hem at 0.474..0.546 and her left's at 0.514..
0.586, against the panel measurements 0.442..0.520 and 0.486..0.556 already
recorded in the header of pants.ts -- the whole rag was ~28 mm too high and had
been since round 1, because the comment above the table describes hemY+offset as
the lowest point at the BACK while the two numbers it was fitted to are FRONT
readings. hemY 0.466 -> 0.438 lands the front hems on 0.446..0.518 (her right)
and 0.486..0.558 (her left), i.e. within 4 mm of both measurements.
The hip wrap, the khaki canvas apron and the pocket sewn on it.
ROUND 2 -- three numbers changed, all read off the TEXTURED panels at 4x
with tools/grid.py --metres, because the mauve, the khaki and the striped
trousers are three different colours and the clay panels are not.
1. THE MAUVE IS ON HER RIGHT ONLY, so `splitX` cuts the wrap at the
midline. body_2 (front): unstriped mauve fills image-left from the belt
down over her right hip, while her left hip is striped trousers.
body_5 (back): unstriped mauve over her right buttock, khaki over her
left. There is no mauve anywhere on her left in either panel. A closed
barrel puts 14 mm of cloth round a half of the figure that has none.
2. THE FLAP HANGS TO y = 0.815, not 0.912. On body_2 at 4x the flap's
cream-piped hem is a rounded corner ON the silhouette at y = 0.815,
climbing inboard and up to the belt at about x = -0.06, y = 1.03.
Round 1 read 0.912 off the same panel: at y = 0.94..0.84 the front
silhouette carries a SECOND run at x = -0.17..-0.23 which is her right
forearm hanging free, and the gap between it and the body was mistaken
for the hem. On body_5 the same hem crosses her right rear at
y = 0.945, so the low corner is FORWARD of her side -- bearing ~ -1.1,
where it is nearly on the front silhouette but hidden behind the hip
from behind. `flapHem` is that curve; the wrap's own `hem` stays
20-100 mm above it so both edges show and the cloth reads as folded.
Low at the front on her right and climbing to the rear IS the spiral;
a single tilted plane cannot make it.
3. THE APRON RUNS ROUND TO HER LEFT REAR. body_5 shows khaki from her
left flank across to the spine, hem at y ~ 0.985, so `wedge` now spans
-0.68 .. 2.90 rad. That is wider than pi, which one pair of half-planes
cannot express, so the build unions two overlapping wedges.
4. FLAP STAND-OFF, tuned against the scoreboard, not guessed. `flapOut` is
how far the free end stands off the wrap under it. Swept 0 / 2 / 4 / 7 mm
with everything else fixed, seven bakes back to back so no other author's
edit could drift between them (round 1 and round 2 repeated as sentinels,
and they reproduced to 0.00): score 41.37 / 41.40 / 40.89 / 41.03 against
round 1's 41.33. It is knife-edged at 4 mm because compare.py's shoulder
landmark flips there -- 82 mm of figure height, from a hip apron -- so 2 mm
is chosen as the wide, flat optimum rather than the peak of a spike.
The same seven-bake harness ablated the three changes above: the midline
cut is worth +0.12, the long flap moves width +0.004 and IoU +0.0005, and
the apron's reach to her left rear costs 0.13 -- ALL of it the same yaw-45
shoulder flip, with IoU and the colour term both preferring the longer
band. It is kept because body_5 shows the khaki there. Shorten
canvas.wedge[1] from 2.90 to 1.85 to buy that 0.13 back if the landmark
term is ever weighted higher.
Heights, panel by panel (metre grid keyed to each alpha bbox):
body_3  wrap top edge, her right hip                       y = 1.091
body_2  flap low corner, her right front (4x, piped hem)   y = 0.815
body_5  flap hem, her right rear                           y = 0.945
body_5  wrap hem near the spine                            y ~ 1.02
body_2  apron lower edge, front centre                     y = 0.991
body_2  apron lower edge, her left front (deepest)         y = 0.930
body_5  apron lower edge, her left rear                    y = 0.985
The apron: body_1 at 4.5x shows its top edge tucked UNDER the studded hip
belt and its lower edge a smooth curve. Lower edge in the front view,
`topY`/`topTiltX` are the reference's own near-level top edge, and the
build takes the LOWER of that and the hip belt's underside (belts.json:
hipY - beltWidth/2 + hipTilt*x) plus `tuck`, so the raw edge stays behind
the belt without following its 0.29 tilt up her left hip. `round` fillets
the band's two ends, which is what stops them reading as tears.
`backing` is negative: the wrap follows the apron down and past it by 6 mm,
so the apron's free edge is an 8 mm step onto cloth, not a 23 mm cliff onto
the trousers.
sashCloth: the reference's flap is a lighter, UNSTRIPED mauve. Sampled
adjacent surfaces on body_3 give flap 0.337 0.188 0.298 against pants seat
0.278 0.176 0.231, i.e. the flap is +21/+7/+29 % on the same lighting, and
applying that lift to the palette's own pants colour gives 0.400 0.209
0.381. The value here splits those two derivations. Striped pants read
0.310 0.180 0.275 through the stripes, so the wrap must carry no stripes --
that colour break is what makes the one-sided flap read at all.
ROUND 3 -- VERIFIED, NOT CHANGED. The round-3 brief asked whether this part
was holding the legs apart in the front outline. It is not, and the number
behind that finding does not survive a look:
a. The lowest cloth this part puts anywhere is the flap hem's corner at
y = 0.815, which is the measurement above off body_2. Everything else
bottoms out at 0.931 (wrap, following the apron down by `backing`) or
0.937 (apron). Nothing this part builds reaches the legs at all.
b. The full-figure front render does carry extra silhouette runs between
t = 0.388 and 0.512, but tools/pants_probe.py puts them at +7.1..+12.2
%H of figure height from the centroid -- her LEFT hand and the Zapper on
that hip, on the far side of the figure from this wrap. clay_2 carries
the same detachment on the other side (a run at -13.4..-10.2 %H at
t = 0.512, her right hand). Between t = 0.237 and 0.362 -- the trouser
legs -- the render is one run, exactly as clay_2 is.
c. Where the reference's outline genuinely IS open and ours is not is the
BACK view, from y = 0.49 to 0.75, and that gap is closed by body.json's
blendLeg 0.028 smooth-unioning the two legs, not by any garment.
Narrowing the seat was tried anyway, since this part rides on the trousers'
own blouse: scaling `pants.flare` above y = 0.78 by 0.75 and 0.55 in two
back-to-back whole-figure bakes cost 0.16 and 1.55 of score and 0.0015 and
0.0041 of mean IoU. The hip is the width the reference has; reverted.
Read off ref/views/clay_2.png + body_2.png (front), body_0.png (her left
side, the one with the pistol) and clay_5.png (back), with a metre grid
keyed to the alpha bbox (figure 1.72 m tall).
SIDES follow docs/HANDEDNESS.md, not the older text in PART_CONTRACT.md:
screen-right in a front view is +X, and the front panel puts the Zapper,
the two arm bands and the drop-leg rig on image-right, so all three are
+X, her LEFT. The tattooed arm is the bare one, -X. Cross-checked here:
body_0 (her left side) shows the pistol and an untattooed upper arm with
both bands and their brass buckles; body_4 (her right side) shows the
cloud sleeve and no bands. rigSide flips the thigh strap, the holster, the
arm bands and the long glove sleeve together if that is ever mirrored.
Hip belt: the front run climbs from y=1.020 at image-left to y=1.100 at
image-right (the rig side), a plane tilt of 0.29 about z through y=1.062
at the centre; the band measures 33-35 mm tall on body_0, between y=1.070
Slung strap: clay_5 shows it crossing the back diagonally about 25 mm
under the belt on the rig hip and dropping to y=0.90 on the other side --
tilt 0.50 through y=1.004. Both drop straps hang off it.
Thigh strap at y=0.855 (body_0 shows the band between 0.845 and 0.875).
Arm bands, measured on clay_2/body_2 at 9x and confirmed on body_0: the
upper band spans 1.250-1.283 and the lower 1.213-1.247, so 32 mm wide at
centres 1.266 and 1.230. The base spec's lower band at 1.196 is 34 mm too
low -- that height is the top hem of the sleeve on that arm, not a band.
hipR from the base spec is unused: the loop radius is torsoHalfWidth(y)
plus hipPadX/hipPadZ, then pushed out until it clears the trousers and the
hip wrap, capped by hipMaxPush. The thigh strap and the arm bands are
fitted to the dressed limb the same way rather than to a spec radius.
Fingerless black gloves. Measured on ref/views/body_2.png with a metre grid
Sides follow docs/HANDEDNESS.md: +X is her left and is the side of the
Zapper, the arm bands and the long sleeve; the tattooed arm is -X.
keyed to the alpha bbox; panel x is mirrored with respect to this frame.
The two arms differ on the sheet: on the tattooed arm (image-left, -X) the
sleeve is cut at y=1.115 and on the Zapper-side arm (image-right, +X) it runs
up over the elbow to y=1.208, right under the lower black band. topY is
the short one, longTopY the long one, and belts.rigSide decides which
arm gets which so the pair follows if the bands are mirrored.
The base spec's topY of 1.052 is a third of the way up the forearm, not
'most of' it: the wrist joint is at y=0.988 and the elbow at 1.181.
The rolled wrist cuff reads between y=0.945 and y=0.990 on the sheet, so
cuffY 0.966 with cuffWidth 0.044.
knuckleT is in units of the wrist->hand vector: body.ts runs the finger
stub out to 1.42, and the cut at 1.14 leaves the last third bare, which
matches the bare fingers below y=0.885 on the sheet.
Measured off clay_0/clay_4 (side: sole stack, cuff hang, throat wall),
clay_5 (back: cuff wings, and how close the two cuffs come to touching),

ROUND 3.  Everything below marked R3 was re-read with a per-row run
decomposition of the panel (out/boots_probe.py) rather than by eye off a
grid, and measured against the same decomposition of the render
(out/boots_raw.py, which reads a --frame 1.80 preview in its own metric
frame).  Two structural corrections came out of it.
R3-A  THE POSE.  skel.ankleL is 47 mm above and 28 mm in front of
skel.ankleR.  place() used to translate y by a literal 0, so both
boots stood on the world floor and the stagger vanished.  On clay_2
the bottom 47 mm of the figure is ONE run -- her right boot alone,
0.103 m wide at y = 0.02 and 0.114 at 0.04 -- and the left boot only
joins in at y = 0.047.  The render had two boots there, merging into
one 0.31 m run at yaw 315 against the sheet's 0.11.
R3-B  THE CUFF IS WIDEST AT THE FOLD, NOT AT THE HEM.  Following the
planted boot's own axis on clay_2 (x = -0.060 at y = 0.20 drifting to
y = 0.20   run -0.123..+0.061   outer reach 0.063   the hem
y = 0.30   run -0.146..+0.126   outer reach 0.091   the fold
so laterally the collar GROWS on the way up.  Fore and aft clay_0
says the opposite -- 0.230 deep at y = 0.195 against 0.178 at 0.295.
Both earlier versions had the lateral relation inverted and flared
the collar down and out into a bell, which is the pancake the review
measured.  foldHalf* and rimHalf* are now two separate superellipse
outlines instead of one plus an anisotropic interpolation weight.

the two boots covers z in [c*zMin - s*halfW, c*zMax + s*halfW] with

WHAT THE PANELS WILL NOT AGREE ON.  A boot 0.20 long and 0.09 wide cannot
project narrower than about 0.19 at 45 degrees off its own axis, yet clay_1
and clay_3 both read the boot at 0.10-0.11 in the bottom 0.08 m -- the same
width clay_2 reads dead ahead.  The two side panels disagree with each
other the same way: clay_0 shows the two boots almost coincident (0.239
total at y = 0.04) and clay_4 shows them 0.15 m apart fore-and-aft (0.361).
The turnaround is a perspective sheet whose intermediate panels are not at
45 degrees and whose camera pitch varies, so the three-quarter boot widths
are not a reachable target for an orthographic render at a pinned yaw.
What IS reachable there, and what round 3 goes after, is the run STRUCTURE:
one boot at the floor rather than two, and a boot mass that carries up to
y = 0.33 instead of stopping at 0.29.
Local frame: authored around the ankle's ground projection with +z toward
the toe, then yawed by pose.footToeOut and dropped onto skel.ankle{L,R} at
that ankle's own height.
The Zapper, holstered barrel-down on her LEFT thigh (+X). Round 1 had it
on -X, her right; docs/HANDEDNESS.md is the record -- the gun is visible in
body_0 (her left side) and absent from body_4 (her right side).
Authored in a gun-local frame: +Y up the gun from muzzle to grip, +Z the
gun's front (the barrel-rail side), +X outboard across the flat.
`anchor` is where the tank's centre lands in world metres; `pitch` tips the
grip forward (+Z) and a NEGATIVE `roll` tips it outboard (+X).

materials.$comment: Colours are sRGB display values in 0..1 -- authored to match medians sampled off ref/views/body_2.png, so a renderer must convert them to linear before lighting. They are sampled from the artist's RENDER, not from an albedo, so they carry a little of its lighting; that is a deliberate approximation and it is why the viewer's exposure is calibrated against the same sheet.

lod.$comment: Voxel size in metres. Triangle count scales as 1/voxel^2: measured 249k tris at 6.0 mm, so 4.5 mm lands near 440k and keeps the three LODs together under the 16 MB an artifact can carry.

$comment: Numbers body.ts needs that spec.widths does not carry, all read off
ref/views/clay_2.png (front) and clay_0.png (her left side) with a metre
grid keyed to each panel's alpha bbox (bbox top = 1.72 m, bottom = 0).
yoke[] is [y, halfX, halfZ, centreZ] and takes over from torsoHalfWidth()
above yokeY0.  It exists because the spec's own width table ends with a
single key at neckBase whose radius is neckR*1.9 = 0.068, so any loft
through it caps off with a 137 mm ball at the throat -- which is what both
top.ts and choker.ts had to build their own neck columns to work around.
Above y = 1.42 this column is head.json's neck extended down, exactly as
top.json's neckCol* and choker.json's neck* already assume: r 0.0435 at
1.420 tapering to 0.040 at 1.525, squashZ 1.1, centre z 0.0076 -> -0.012.
Measured, front silhouette on her left (screen-right, the side the hair
does not cover), half-width from the midline: 0.041 at y = 1.490 (the
neck, agreeing with the 0.040 in MEASUREMENTS.md), 0.076 at 1.440,
1.360.  The column carries the inner half of that and trap[] the ramp.
Side view, front edge referred to the chest front at y = 1.360: the throat
at 1.429 sits 51 mm behind it and the clavicle at 1.402 sits 31 mm behind
